text: Refined depth and operating controls (1D-3062m-boiler-electric-chp-screw, R0193): accept. Lower LCOE and lower CO2 while meeting every hard rule with the geothermal outage covering the heating peak.
Centrifugal chiller with cooling tower (1D-3062m-boiler-electric-chp-tower, R0205): alternative. Lower CO2 but higher LCOE after including the requested carbon price.
Seasonal pit heat storage (1D-3125m-boiler-electric-chp-screw-pit250k, R0192): alternative. Lower CO2 and purchased gas consumption, but higher capital cost and LCOE.

Best tested winter-outage design is R0193: geothermal doublet, boiler backup, electric screw chiller with dry cooler, associated-gas CHP and operating rules. Carbon price is 180 EUR/t, incorporating the user's additional 100 above the existing 80. Common geothermal outage starts on day 1 and includes the heating peak. All annual hard rules pass, and the operating-day native Solver cross-check agrees. R0207 directly confirms feasibility at lower permeability with operating_rules retained; sensitivity's nominal-permeability rerun did not reproduce R0193, so avoid treating that sensitivity series as an exact controlled comparison. Loaded measured weather was used in the free-cooling and ATES studies.
